question.prompt: Line \(\ell\) in the coordinate plane has the equation \(3x - 5y + 40 = 0.\) This line is rotated \(45^\circ\) counterclockwise about the point \((20, 20)\) to obtain line \(k.\) What is the \(x\)-coordinate of the \(x\)-intercept of line \(k?\)

solutions.title: Bisect a right angle
solutions.explanation:
The rotation center lies on the original line, so finding the rotated line only requires finding its new direction.

Let \(P=(20,20)\). Since
\[
3(20)-5(20)+40=0,
\]
\(P\) lies on \(\ell\) and remains fixed during the rotation. Another point on \(\ell\) is \(Q=(25,23)\), giving the displacement vector \(\overrightarrow{PQ}=(5,3)\).

A \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise turn changes a displacement \((u,v)\) to \((-v,u)\). Thus the \(90^\circ\) image of \(Q\) about \(P\) is
\[
R=P+(-3,5)=(17,25).
\]
Consequently, \(PQ=PR\) and \(\angle QPR=90^\circ\).

Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(QR\). Its coordinates are
\[
M=\left(\frac{25+17}{2},\frac{23+25}{2}\right)=(21,24).
\]
In the isosceles triangle \(PQR\), the segment \(PM\) bisects the angle at \(P\). Therefore, ray \(PM\) is \(45^\circ\) counterclockwise from ray \(PQ\), so \(k\) is the line through \(P\) and \(M\).

The displacement from \(P\) to \(M\) is \((1,4)\), giving slope \(4\). Hence
\[
y-20=4(x-20).
\]
At the \(x\)-intercept, \(y=0\), so \(-20=4(x-20)\), yielding \(\boxed{15}\), choice \(\textbf{B}\).

solutions.title: Use tangent addition
solutions.explanation:
A counterclockwise rotation adds \(45^\circ\) to the line's direction angle, so the tangent addition formula gives the new slope.

Rewriting the original equation gives
\[
y=\frac35x+8.
\]
Let \(\theta\) be its acute angle with the positive \(x\)-axis. Then \(\tan\theta=\frac35\). The slope of the rotated line is
\[
\tan(\theta+45^\circ)
=\frac{\tan\theta+\tan45^\circ}{1-\tan\theta\tan45^\circ}
=\frac{\frac35+1}{1-\frac35}
=4.
\]

The point \(P=(20,20)\) satisfies the original equation because \(60-100+40=0\). Since \(P\) is the rotation center, it also lies on \(k\). Thus
\[
y-20=4(x-20).
\]
Setting \(y=0\) gives \(x-20=-5\), so the requested coordinate is \(\boxed{15}\), choice \(\textbf{B}\).
